question_text: Does longer empty-bed contact time necessarily translate into better PFAS performance in granular activated carbon systems?

question_components.description: Determine whether increasing empty-bed contact time (EBCT) in granular activated carbon systems for PFAS removal necessarily improves PFAS performance, including effects on breakthrough behavior, adsorption capacity, and removal efficiency, and whether there are conditions where longer EBCT does not increase performance.

validated_chunk_tags.exact_support: Higher empty bed contact time (EBCT) caused steeper PFAS breakthrough curves with respect to throughput, but did not affect apparent adsorption capacity.
Consistent differences in PFAA adsorption capacity were not observed for empty bed contact times of 13 and 26 min in full-scale adsorbers treating GW.
Longer EBCTs caused steeper PFAS breakthroughs with respect to throughput for F400 while having very similar BV 50.

Recently, McCleaf et al. conducted a pilot-scale GAC adsorber test with an empty bed contact time (EBCT) of 6.1 min for assessing the breakthrough of 14 PFAS spiked in groundwater ( McCleaf et al., 2017). Another recent pilot-scale study employed an EBCT of 10 min for 10 PFAS in groundwater ( Liu et al., 2019 ).

For example, for remediation, the typical empty bed contact time (EBCT) might be in the order of 10–20 min (AWWA, 2019; Belkouteb et al., 2020; Gagliano et al., 2020), whereas typical filter- adsorbers for drinking water production might employ somewhat shorter EBCTs in the order of 5 –10 min ( Graese et al., 1987 ).

Traditional full-scale GAC treatment facility design is typically based on empty bed contact time (EBCT) and media service-life, often described by the number of bed volumes (BVs) the system can treat until solute breakthrough ( Crittenden et al., 1987 ).
